headline: GPT-6 Astra Edits Model Weights Directly
summary: MIT CSAIL reported a weight-space programming method in which GPT-6 Astra edited a smaller model's weights directly instead of retraining it. The result sharply improved math and instruction-following performance, suggesting a new way to patch model behavior without training runs.

headline: Hydrogen-1.0 Open-Weight Science Model Released
summary: Deep Principle released Hydrogen-1.0, a fully open 753B-parameter science model under an MIT license. The model is positioned as a research-focused system for planning experiments, debugging simulations, and finding materials candidates, with benchmark claims against GPT-6-Astra.

headline: Open-Source Gpu-Unlock Boosts GeForce Tensor Core Performance
summary: An open-source tool called gpu-unlock reportedly removes NVIDIA's GeForce Tensor Core performance limits. The repo claims up to 87% faster AI workloads on consumer GPUs, though it remains Linux-only and experimental.

headline: Anthropic Lets Claude Auto-Connect Plugins Without Re-Authorization
summary: Anthropic added enterprise-managed authorization so Claude can auto-connect plugins without repeated re-authorization. The change reduces friction for enterprise deployments using MCP-based integrations.

headline: Study Tests Whether Claude Code Can Improve Itself
summary: A study examined whether Claude Code can improve by reviewing its own past mistakes. The result was presented as a reality check on how hard it is for models to judge whether their suggestions actually work.

headline: Google Releases Open Multimodal Embedding Model
summary: Google released an open multimodal embedding model that the newsletter says beats models 12 times its size. The result suggests a strong efficiency gain for multimodal retrieval and embedding use cases.

headline: Ist-Daslab Compresses 763B Deepseek Coding Model To 72 Gb
summary: IST-DASLab released a compressed version of a 763B DeepSeek coding model that fits into 72 GB at 1 bit per parameter. The release underscores how aggressively large models can now be quantized for practical use.

headline: OpenAI Quadruples Bug Bounty Payouts To $172,000
summary: OpenAI raised its bug bounty payouts, offering up to $172,000 for a critical finding. The move is meant to harden OpenAI's platform by incentivizing external security research.

headline: Route Anything: A Study Of Model And Policy Routing For General-Purpose AI Systems
summary: A new framework studies how to route tasks across specialized models, tools, and policies in general-purpose AI systems. The work introduces an omni-modal trajectory matrix spanning 25 benchmarks and reports gains from oracle and learned routing.

headline: Think Less, Locally: Local Preference Learning For Reasoning Compression
summary: Tencent-linked researchers propose LoCo, a method for teaching reasoning models when to stop deliberating. The approach reduces output length substantially while maintaining or improving accuracy on math and code benchmarks.

headline: Words Caught In The Heart: Simulating Person-Specific Expression For Self-Opaque Clients In Psychotherapy
summary: Researchers propose Pandora, a psychotherapy client simulation framework that models psychological and relational state to generate more individualized responses. In evaluations, it achieved the highest expression similarity and disclosure-alignment scores among compared systems.

headline: MoviEdit: Long-Form Multi-Shot Video Editing Made Easy
summary: Adobe researchers introduce MoviEdit, an end-to-end framework for scalable long-form multi-shot video editing. The work also introduces a new benchmark and a large automatically generated training set.

headline: Behind Video Generation: Observations And Insights On Multimodal Understanding From Kling
summary: KlingAI Research presents observations on the multimodal understanding stack behind controllable video generation. The report covers captioning, prompt enhancement, text encoders, reward modeling, and evaluation protocols.

headline: Grok Bot Starts Making Phone Calls
summary: SpaceXSI rolled out phone-calling in Grok Bot for paid users, letting the agent sit on hold, book appointments, and negotiate bills on U.S. numbers. The feature pushes AI agents further into real-world tasks, but users remain legally responsible for every call the bot makes.

headline: Midterm Voters Turn Against Data Centers And AI
summary: Voters in U.S. midterms backed limits on data centers in nearly every local measure that appeared on ballots, while exit polling showed broad skepticism about AI. The result suggests growing public resistance to AI infrastructure and tougher scrutiny ahead for the industry.

headline: Keith Built An AI Archive Of Handwritten Family Letters
summary: A reader built a searchable family archive for handwritten 1940s letters and photos using Google AI Studio, Replit, Firebase, and AI chat. The workflow shows how people are using AI to preserve personal history and make scanned documents queryable.

headline: Introducing Pangram Image 1.0
summary: Pangram Image 1.0 is an AI image and AI video detection model that produces heatmaps localizing where AI appears in media. It also includes a Chrome extension and API support for images and video.

headline: Ripple-65B Preview
summary: Ripple-65B Preview is a frontier open-weight model that tops TerminalBench 2.1 and beats several much larger open-weight models. It was trained for $32 million and is available on Hugging Face, Together AI, GMI Cloud, and OpenRouter.

headline: OpenAI To Acquire Pierre Computer Company, Inc.
summary: OpenAI will acquire Pierre Computer Company to enhance Codex's developer tools, including Code Storage and other open-source projects. The deal is a strategic move tied to OpenAI's coding product stack.

headline: Conductor Is Joining Meta
summary: AI coding startup Conductor is joining Meta, bringing its multi-agent management platform into the company. The move highlights Meta’s continued interest in agent tooling.

headline: Token Spend Is Exploding, But Value Is Harder To Measure
summary: The piece argues that rising token usage is a poor proxy for actual productivity or AI value, even as token volumes surge across companies and platforms. It contrasts internal token burn incentives with broader market growth and asks whether spend is translating into useful work.

headline: Frontier Model Edited Another Model's Weights And 6x'd Its Math Score
summary: MIT CSAIL researchers published Weight-Space Programming, showing that a frontier model can read, repair, and write neural network weights directly without a training loop. In one result, GPT-6 Astra edited 131,072 weights in Qwen3.5-0.8B and pushed MATH-500 from 7.9% to 48.1%.

headline: Anthropic Discloses $16.96 Billion Quarterly Revenue And Huge Compute Commitments
summary: Anthropic's amended S-1 says Q3 revenue reached $16.96 billion, while compute and infrastructure costs and long-term commitments remain enormous. The filing also says the company may imminently meet its Responsible Scaling Policy definition of dramatically accelerated progress attributable to AI.

headline: OpenAI Partners With Cathedral For Internal Security Sprint
summary: OpenAI said it is partnering with Cathedral for its next internal security sprint. The move comes after Cathedral had recently found its way into Anthropic's internal systems through Anthropic's bug bounty program.

headline: Anthropic Turns On Plugin Auto-Connect
summary: Anthropic enabled plugin auto-connect for MCP servers that accept Claude as a trusted issuer. The change removes a re-authorization step at login for supported plugins.

headline: Soniox Ships STT V6
summary: Soniox released STT v6, a speech recognition update covering more than 60 languages. It can filter out the voice agent's own audio and is available in real time and async.

headline: Netflix Is Testing An AI Discover Tab
summary: Netflix is testing an AI Discover tab on supported U.S. TVs. The feature recommends what to watch based on mood.

headline: Sonos Opens U.S. Waitlist For 27voice Assistant
summary: Sonos opened a U.S. waitlist for its 27voice assistant. Early access begins November 12, with the waitlist opening on November 6.

headline: TextKit
summary: Send and receive texts in the US and Canada through a simple API. The product positions itself as an infrastructure tool for building SMS workflows.

headline: Polylane For Google Cloud
summary: An AI on-call engineer for Google Cloud apps. It is positioned as a developer tool for monitoring and handling cloud app issues.

headline: Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe
summary: Intelligent transcription with a speech LLM. The product appears to add speech-to-text capabilities powered by NVIDIA's Nemotron line.

headline: FounderMail
summary: Mail for you and your agents on a Cloudflare domain. It is presented as an email tool for founders and automated agents.

headline: CC Auto Review
summary: A macOS app that reviews GitHub pull requests with local Claude Code. It targets developer workflows around code review.

headline: Scrollsnacks
summary: Launch videos broken down second by second. The product helps users analyze video pacing and structure.

headline: Claude Code Cuts Background Subagent Token Cost By 99% In V2.1.316
summary: Claude Code v2.1.316 reduces background subagent status-update token costs by 99% by having Haiku 5.5 generate updates from short notes instead of rereading full conversation history. Anthropic says this lowers background-subagent usage by about 5% and gives roughly 6% more prompts on the same plan.

headline: OpenAI's Images 2.6 Adds GIF Creation To ChatGPT
summary: OpenAI released Images 2.6, a faster image model family rolling out across ChatGPT and Codex with built-in GIF capabilities. Developers can access two API versions, and users can turn typed ideas, photos, or sketches into animations.

headline: Kimi K3.1 Pro
summary: Moonshot AI released Kimi K3.1 Pro, a multimodal model with a million-token context window. The model is described as improving coding, 3D creation, and factual accuracy.

headline: How OpenAI Patched 948 Linux Vulnerabilities
summary: OpenAI described an autonomous pipeline for discovering, exploiting, and patching security vulnerabilities. In one run, its cybersecurity model validated and generated patches for 948 Linux local privilege escalation vulnerabilities.

headline: Google Cloud Announces 80,000-GPU A5X Cluster
summary: Google Cloud says A5X instances powered by NVIDIA Vera Rubin are now available, backed by an 80,000-GPU data center. The announcement signals a major infrastructure move for large-scale AI workloads.

headline: Tsinghua And NVIDIA Release Benchmark For 37 Interactive Video Models
summary: Tsinghua and NVIDIA released an open-source benchmark evaluating 37 interactive video models. The benchmark adds a comparative dataset for assessing interactive video systems.

headline: LeCun Paper Argues Models Converge To The Same World View
summary: A paper by LeCun argues that AI models trained on different data converge to the same world view. The work is presented as a technical claim about representation and convergence across training data.

headline: Yarchi Ships Open-Source Site For Teaching AI Agents
summary: Yarchi released a free open-source site that teaches AI agents in 15 minutes. The project is positioned as a quick educational tool for agent workflows.

headline: Open-Source Tool Runs Full macOS Inside The Terminal
summary: A free open-source tool now runs a full macOS inside a terminal for AI agents. The tool expands the kinds of environments agents can interact with locally.

headline: From Pixels To Actions - Towards Native Vision-Language-Action Policies
summary: NEO-VLA is a structurally encoder-free vision-language-action framework that lets images evolve jointly with language throughout the backbone. The paper argues this improves manipulation robustness and shows native architectures outperform encoder-based counterparts in controlled comparisons.

headline: Turns Matter: Advancing Streaming Video RL Via Turn-Level Credit
summary: TurnWise is a turn-level GRPO framework for streaming video understanding that assigns credit to each decision instead of a single trajectory-level advantage. The method is designed to reduce redundant replies and improve learning from repeated observe/respond decisions.

headline: GameVerse: A Minute-Scale Gameplay Dataset For Long-Horizon Interactive World Modeling
summary: GameVerse is a minute-scale gameplay video dataset built to support long-horizon interactive world modeling. It includes 69.7K clips and 1,358 hours of continuous two-minute sequences, which the authors say substantially extends the temporal horizon of trained models.

headline: FrontierPhysics: Evaluating Agents For End-To-End Physics Research
summary: FrontierPhysics is an end-to-end benchmark for AI agents doing real physics research, not just answering fixed questions. It evaluates literature review, research planning, experimentation, manuscript production, and whether the output is publishable.

headline: What Does Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning Really Improve In LLM Agents?
summary: This paper studies how multi-turn agentic reinforcement learning depends on interaction budgets and finds its gains are not uniform. The authors introduce BudgetMix RL to improve robustness across different execution settings.

headline: METR Finds Anthropic’s AI R&D Capabilities Index Grew 1.9x Faster
summary: METR’s assessment found Anthropic’s internal capabilities index grew at 1.9 times its pre-October 2025 rate, with a 95% confidence interval of 1.5x to 2.8x. Anthropic redacted much of the evidence, and a planned verification of compute allocation was canceled midway.

headline: Granola Launches Voice Typing
summary: Granola launched Voice Typing, letting users hold Fn and dictate clean text into any app. The feature is available now on Mac and Windows, with iOS and Android coming soon.

headline: Google Rolls Out Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash
summary: Google released Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash and cut its video model price by 30%. The update also extends clips from 10 seconds to 15 seconds.

headline: Anthropic Introduces Personal Finance Tool For Claude
summary: Anthropic introduced a new Personal Finance tool for Claude that can connect to users' financial accounts. The assistant can answer questions and provide tailored financial information.

headline: Perplexity Announces Teammates For Perplexity Computer
summary: Perplexity announced Teammates, new AI agents on its Perplexity Computer platform that each own an ongoing project. CEO Aravind Srinivas said he expects every organization to have hundreds of teammates working for each person.

headline: Tokens, Tokens, Tokens
summary: An explainer argues that token spend is a poor proxy for AI value, even as token usage explodes across companies and platforms. It contrasts internal corporate token burn with broader market growth and suggests useful work per unit of energy is the better metric.

headline: ChatGPT Images 2.6 Adds Animated GIFs And Persistent References
summary: OpenAI released ChatGPT Images 2.6, which can generate animated GIFs from prompts or photos and keep reference images persistent. The API also includes Flare and Sunburst variants.

headline: OpenAI Ships First Model Rated Critical For Cyber
summary: OpenAI released GPT-6 Cyber and classified it as Critical under its Preparedness Framework, the top cyber tier. OpenAI says the model outperformed its predecessor on ExploitGym and uncovered 81 previously unknown high-severity Firefox vulnerabilities.

headline: Data Centers Lost 40 Of 41 Ballot Measures
summary: Voters rejected restrictions or approved bans on data center development in 40 of 41 ballot measures across ten states. The results could slow and raise the cost of future data center buildouts.

headline: Anthropic Rolls Out Prompt And Pre-Tool-Call Hooks
summary: Anthropic shipped hooks that route prompts and proposed tool calls through existing DLP vendors before execution. The company says the change makes it easier for enterprises to deploy Claude without exposing sensitive data.

headline: Claude Code Background Agents Switch Status Updates To Haiku 5.5
summary: Claude Code background agents now use Haiku 5.5 for status updates instead of the session model. Anthropic says the change cuts cost per update by about 99% and trims roughly 5% off session allowance use.

headline: Notion Opens Shared Memory For Assistants
summary: Notion opened shared memory so ChatGPT, Claude and other assistants can read the same workspace context. The change is aimed at reducing fragmented agent context across multiple tools.

headline: ElevenLabs Adds Native Enterprise Connectors To ElevenAgents
summary: ElevenAgents added native connectors for NiCE CXone, Genesys Cloud, Amazon Connect and Five9. The update expands its enterprise contact-center integrations.

headline: Pangram Image 1.0 Detects AI-Generated Images With Heatmaps
summary: Pangram Image 1.0 can detect AI-generated images and show heatmaps indicating where it is confident. The visual explanations are intended to make detection results easier to interpret.

headline: Grok Bot Demoed Canceling A Subscription Over The Phone
summary: xAI demoed Grok Bot canceling a subscription over the phone after user approval. The demo shows a consumer agent handling a real-world phone task.

headline: OpenAI Launches Images 2.6 With GIFs And Image Reference
summary: OpenAI is rolling out Images 2.6 globally in ChatGPT and Codex. The model generates images 50% faster than the previous iteration and can create GIFs with speed controls, frame editing, and sharing, while GPT-Image-2.6 Flare and Sunburst are now available through the API.

headline: The Stacks Project, Formalized In Lean
summary: Axiom released a Lean formalization of the entire Stacks Project, a foundational open-source reference in algebraic geometry. The release makes the full mathematical development available as a single machine-checked library for researchers and AI agents.

headline: Cognition Introduces SWE-2 Flash
summary: Cognition introduced SWE-2 Flash, a coding model that uses a new mid-training stage before reinforcement learning. The post frames it as a tooling/model update rather than a standalone launch.

headline: Tencent Launches Hy4
summary: Tencent launched Hy4, a visual language model that supports image processing, chart analysis, and mathematical visual reasoning. Tencent says model weights and system cards will be released in the coming days.

headline: AlphaEvolve GitHub Repo
summary: Google DeepMind released a GitHub repository for AlphaEvolve, a Gemini-powered coding agent for designing advanced algorithms. The repo includes a minimal implementation plus code and data related to discovered solutions.

headline: H-Nets Learn Directly From Raw Bytes
summary: Cartesia’s H-Nets are a new model architecture that learns from raw bytes and matches benchmark performance with less training compute. The item is presented as a technical tooling/research update.

headline: Meta Acquires AI Coding Startup Conductor
summary: Meta acquired Conductor, a startup that lets developers run multiple AI coding agents in parallel workspaces. The move expands Meta's activity in AI coding tools.

headline: Cat Wu Joins OpenAI
summary: Cat Wu has joined OpenAI to build reliable agents that keep users in control. The item is a hiring move at a Tier 1 company.

headline: Together Compiler: Continual Compilation For AI Inference
summary: Together AI introduced Together Compiler, a continual optimization loop for improving inference workloads with high-throughput agents. The release is a developer/tooling update.

headline: Web Grounding For The Decisions API
summary: Perplexity's Decisions API can now search the web before answering. The update adds web grounding to an existing API.

headline: Cloptima
summary: AI Gateway, Guardrails & LLM FinOps.

headline: Plainmail
summary: Real email on every domain you own, for $5 a month flat.

headline: Kivo
summary: Free on-device dictation for any Mac app and AI agent.

headline: Translucent AI
summary: Test infrastructure for hardware teams.

headline: Wisp
summary: Wisp is a little AI fairy who lives on your desktop.

headline: OpenAI Releases GPT-6 Cyber
summary: OpenAI released GPT-6 Cyber, a security-focused model for offensive and defensive teams. It is positioned as a focused tool for finding, testing, and fixing vulnerabilities in real software.

headline: Fireworks Unveils New Products At Forge
summary: Fireworks unveiled new products at Forge to help companies build AI around their own expertise, data, and tasks. The launches include ultra-fast inference, a desktop product, and managed inference on customer-owned GPUs.

headline: METR Finds Anthropic's AI Is Doubling Its Capability Growth Rate
summary: METR reported that Anthropic's models are improving at roughly 2x their historical rate, with much of the speedup attributed to Anthropic using its own AI tools internally. The report suggests AI-assisted research is now measurably accelerating model development.

headline: Anthropic Used Claude To Map A Mysterious Protein Structure
summary: Anthropic's biology team used Claude to investigate vault particles, a protein structure whose function has remained unclear for decades. The work found vault relatives across bacteria and viruses and reduced structure-mapping time from weeks or months to days.

headline: LivLiv Open-Sources 34 KB Web Character Player
summary: LivLiv open-sourced a 34 KB web character player with lip sync and face tracking. The release is a lightweight open-source tool for interactive character playback in the browser.

headline: Sandbox Quantum Releases Self-Hosted AI Teammates Tool
summary: Sandbox Quantum released an open-source project for self-hosted AI teammates inside Slack, Teams, Discord, and Telegram. The tool supports any model and is designed for multi-app team workflows.

headline: New Open-Source Image-Matching Model Improves 3D Reconstruction
summary: A new open-source image-matching model claims state-of-the-art speed and accuracy for 3D reconstruction. The result is presented as a technical advance rather than a product launch.

headline: Orca Ships 39.8B Coding-Agent Model
summary: Orca released an uncensored 39.8B coding-agent model that runs on a single 16 GB GPU. The model is aimed at local or lower-cost coding-agent use.

headline: Web AI Open-Sources 8B Model With Frontier Coding Scores
summary: Web AI open-sourced an 8B model that it says hits 93% of frontier coding scores. The release adds another open-weight coding model to the ecosystem.

headline: VFlash: Fast, Accurate Visual Planning Via Flash Primitive Decoding
summary: VFlash proposes a faster way to generate visual plans for robotics and autonomous driving by decoding spatial primitives jointly instead of one coordinate token at a time. The paper reports lower prediction errors and about 25x faster generation for 3D point motion forecasting, with a downstream world action model reaching 70.2% average success versus 62.6% for the baseline.

headline: Harness-S: Learning From Sibling Harnesses For Generalizable Agent Training
summary: Harness-S is a training method that rescues failed reinforcement learning rollouts by re-running them under specialized sibling harnesses and transferring the resulting behavior back into one policy. The paper reports improved performance on AppWorld, SWE-Gym, and DBBench when the policy is returned to the original harness.

headline: Random Is Almost Enough? Stable And Low-Cost Benchmark Compression Via BestRand
summary: BestRand is a benchmark-compression method that aims to reduce evaluation cost while keeping scores close to full benchmarks. The paper says it lowers high-error risk by 50.2% and average estimation error by 16.4% while using 51.3% of the construction cost, and extends to 70+ text, multimodal, and agent benchmarks.

headline: WeLM-Image: A Unified Image Generation Model Toward Visual Intelligence
summary: WeLM-Image is a unified image foundation model that combines text-to-image generation, instruction-guided editing, and multi-reference synthesis in one system. The paper says the 1536-resolution model ranks first among evaluated open-source models on PRISM-Bench, Qwen-Image-Bench, and UnicBench, and its distilled WeLM-Image-Turbo variant can generate a 1024x1024 image in 4.98 seconds on a single NVIDIA H20 GPU.

headline: TailSteer: Trajectory-Tail Steering For Drift-Resistant Multi-Turn Image Editing
summary: TailSteer is a final-stage training framework designed to reduce cumulative drift in multi-turn image editing while preserving existing model capabilities. The paper reports that it substantially reduces drift over 15-20 editing turns across the FLUX, SenseNova, and Qwen families.

headline: Latent Sparse Attention Cuts Long-Context Processing Costs
summary: Researchers from Prefrontal AI and ETH Zurich developed Latent Sparse Attention (LSA), which groups attention keys into clusters to speed up search in long contexts. In 10-million-token tests, it improved Qwen’s time to first token by 9.2× and accelerated GLM attention-layer prefill by 22.7× against its sparse-attention baseline.

headline: Egoist AI Passport
summary: Egoist AI Passport lets users securely share their personal data with AI tools.

headline: Arcjet AI Security Models
summary: Arcjet introduced a family of custom-trained security models for coding agents.

headline: Higgsfield Miracle
summary: Higgsfield Miracle lets users edit any part of a video without changing the rest.

headline: ClipsPal
summary: ClipsPal is an AI video editor for talking-head videos.

headline: Product Hunt MCP
summary: Product Hunt MCP brings the Product Hunt community into the assistant users work with.

headline: Agent Clan
summary: Agent Clan lets users command Claude Code and Codex agents with gestures.

headline: Muse Realtime Avatar
summary: Muse Realtime Avatar turns voice chats with Muse into live video calls.

headline: Trace by Context.dev
summary: Trace provides a weekly benchmark for web scraping APIs.

headline: SplatAnything: Gaussian Spacing Normalization for Feed-Forward 3DGS Across Arbitrary Scenes
summary: SplatAnything introduces Gaussian Spacing Normalization (GSNorm) to make supervision more consistent across scene scales and camera configurations. Its benchmark experiments report state-of-the-art feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting performance, with strong gains under substantial scale and viewpoint variation.

headline: P^2-MOPD Accelerates Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation With Parameter Priors
summary: P^2-MOPD jointly optimizes expert-parameter mixing coefficients and student weights during on-policy distillation. Across four domains at 1.7B and 4B scales, it reaches MOPD’s final average recovery in half the training steps; the 1.7B model achieves 94.7% average recovery versus MOPD’s 80.9%.

headline: LongBanana: An Expert-Verified Benchmark for Long-Context Multi-Reference Image Synthesis
summary: LongBanana introduces an expert-designed benchmark for testing long-context, multi-reference image synthesis, along with the LongBanana-Gen agent-harness framework. It includes 90 tasks and 4,670 expert-specified evaluation items; experiments find that a ReAct-Plan-Exec-Reflect workflow can improve generation, with gains depending on the harness.

headline: Beneath the Surface: What We Overlook When We Talk About Agent Evolution
summary: A study of agent-harness evolution finds that benchmark gains can come with losses in previously covered tasks, higher deployment costs, and inconsistent transfer. The authors propose preservation-aware evaluation and revise the EvoAudit process for selecting, analyzing, mutating, and gating agents.

headline: EvoWorld: Towards Out-of-Sight World Evolution in Generative Video Models
summary: EvoWorld combines a vision-language model that tracks and reasons about world state with a segment-autoregressive video renderer to produce event-conditioned world evolution. The paper also introduces EvoWorld-Data and EvoWorld-Bench, reporting improved causal evolution while preserving visual quality and consistency.

headline: Nvidia Board Opens Investigation Into Jensen Huang Intelligence Claims
summary: Nvidia’s board opened an independent investigation into reports that CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort. The board said it has no reason to believe national security or company secrets were compromised, and that Huang is cooperating.

headline: How Anthropic Builds Agent Memory
summary: Anthropic explored a method for AI agents to build long-term memory by recording interaction experiences and reorganizing them during idle periods. The process, called “dreaming,” examines how different memory components help retain and organize useful information.

headline: Higgsfield Previews Miracle Video Editing Feature
summary: Higgsfield previewed Miracle, a feature that separates video into editable layers so users can recolor objects or change on-screen text. It is currently available only to beta testers.

headline: A Proof of the Aaronson-Ambainis Conjecture
summary: A research system developed at PSI using an Anthropic model proved the Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture, a key open problem in quantum complexity theory. The result says quantum computers are not exponentially faster than classical computers on random inputs.

headline: Thinking Machines Lab Releases Inkling 2 Small
summary: Thinking Machines Lab released Inkling 2 Small, a coding and vision model that nears top rivals from DeepSeek and Kimi on coding tests. The lab plans to open-source it next week.

headline: OpenAI Closes About $11 Billion in Funding at $1.25 Trillion Valuation
summary: OpenAI reportedly closed about $11 billion in new funding at a $1.25 trillion valuation, up from its $852 billion valuation in March.

headline: GPT-6 Cyber
summary: OpenAI introduced GPT-6 Cyber, a cybersecurity model designed to identify and validate exploitable vulnerabilities within researcher-defined boundaries.

headline: Introducing Inkling 2 Small
summary: Thinking Machines introduced Inkling 2 Small, a 594B-parameter Mixture-of-Experts model with image input and interactive creation capabilities. It is initially available through Tinker, with full weights planned under Apache 2.0 next week after safety testing and red-teaming.

headline: Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash
summary: Google introduced Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash, an update aimed at improving speed, cost-efficiency, and supported clip lengths for developers.

headline: Cloudflare’s Trust Framework for AI Agents
summary: Cloudflare outlined challenges websites face as AI agents increasingly act on users’ behalf, including verifying identities, assessing trustworthiness, and assigning accountability.

headline: The Benchmark Where AIs Have to Lie to Win
summary: An analysis of AI models playing Blood on the Clocktower examines capabilities such as creative scheming, bluffing, and collective reasoning that other benchmarks do not clearly reveal.

headline: NVIDIA Introduced VFlash
summary: NVIDIA introduced VFlash, a vision model that generates geometric predictions such as robot trajectories and 3D motion in parallel rather than token by token.

headline: New NVIDIA Cosmos 3 Open Models for Interactive World Simulation
summary: NVIDIA’s Cosmos 3 platform now offers four open-weight models for interactive world simulation and driving scenes, each with 16 billion trainable parameters. They support multi-sensor data generation, synchronized observations, and photorealistic video from simulator controls.

headline: Personal Finance in Claude
summary: Anthropic introduced Personal Finance in Claude, allowing users to connect bank and credit card accounts and ask questions about balances, transactions, and spending.

headline: Muse Voice
summary: Meta announced voice conversations and expressive avatars for its Muse app, enabling users to brainstorm, plan trips, and complete tasks through spoken interactions.

headline: Devin Review 2.0
summary: The cost of a Devin Review per pull request has dropped by 82% since August.

headline: Build Live Apps in Cursor and Share Them With a Link
summary: Cursor users can describe a tool and have Cursor build it, set up a database, run security checks, and deploy the app for sharing through a link.

headline: Nous Research Fine-Tunes Qwen3 to Cut Pro-China Propaganda Rate From 22% to 1%
summary: Nous Research fine-tuned Alibaba’s Qwen3.8-27B into Arete-27B, reducing the measured propaganda rate to under 1% while improving its fact score. The weights, evaluation set, and training data are publicly available on Hugging Face.

headline: Sakutto Translates Web Pages Using a Local LLM
summary: Sakutto is a free, open-source Chrome extension that translates web pages on-device using the 0.8B PLaMo 3 Translate model. It supports 53 languages and is available from the Chrome Web Store.

headline: OpenCode Ships Browser Control for Coding Agents
summary: OpenCode Browse lets coding agents control a user’s existing browser tabs and sessions, including authenticated sites. It supports several coding tools and Chromium-based browsers, with interactions kept local.

headline: OpenAI Introduces BioBasicsBench for Wet-Lab Science Tasks
summary: OpenAI introduced BioBasicsBench, a benchmark evaluating AI performance in interpreting raw experimental data from 100 routine wet-lab science tasks.

headline: neuml Ships txtai, an Open-Source Semantic Search and LLM Orchestration Framework
summary: neuml released txtai, an open-source framework combining semantic search and LLM orchestration.

headline: Tencent’s 27B Model Rewrites and Retrains Itself With Zero Human Input
summary: A Tencent research paper presents a 27B model that rewrites and retrains itself using its own outcomes, without human input.

headline: StartLux Releases Decision Models That Think Only When Uncertain
summary: A research paper introduces StartLux decision models ranging from 0.8B to 27B parameters that reason only when uncertain.

headline: New Open-Source Library Renders Live AI Agent Cards in Slack and Teams
summary: Vercel Labs released an open-source library for rendering live AI agent cards inside Slack and Microsoft Teams.

headline: OpenAI Launches GPT-6 Cyber
summary: OpenAI launched GPT-6 Cyber for approved security customers. In a test, it found 948 serious bugs in Linux, at about $1,280 per bug.

headline: ChatGPT Images Adds GIF Creation
summary: OpenAI added GIF creation to ChatGPT Images 2.6, which can turn a prompt or photo into an animated GIF and use reference images to maintain a consistent look. The feature is available on every ChatGPT plan, alongside two new image models for developers.

headline: OpenAI Agrees to Acquire Pierre
summary: OpenAI agreed to acquire Pierre, whose open-source tools already power parts of Codex. Pierre builds storage for code written and edited by AI agents; the price was not disclosed.

headline: Anthropic Says Its Models May Imminently Reach AI-Driven Research Progress
summary: Anthropic’s amended S-1 filing says future models may “imminently” cross the company’s threshold for AI-driven progress, often called recursive self-improvement. The filing also reports Q3 revenue of $16.96 billion, up from $11.56 billion in Q2.

headline: Claude Adds Personal Finance Connections
summary: Claude’s Personal Finance feature connects bank, card, loan, and investment accounts so users can ask questions about their money. It can access up to 24 months of transactions but cannot move money, and is available in the US for now.

headline: Claude Helps Map a Bacterial Vault Particle
summary: Anthropic says Claude helped its biology team map what it calls the first 3D structure of a vault particle from bacterial life. The barrel-shaped structure’s function remains unknown, and a preprint was published November 5.

headline: Google Will Turn Off AI for Student Accounts by Default
summary: Google will keep Gemini, Gemini Notebook, and Search off for student accounts until schools turn them on. The change is rolling out over the coming months.

headline: Google Antigravity Adds Remote Agents
summary: Google’s Antigravity coding app added Remote Agents that run in Google’s cloud and continue working after users close their laptops. They are for AI Pro and Ultra subscribers and run commands without asking by default.

headline: Google’s Omni 1.2 Flash Makes Longer, Cheaper Videos
summary: Omni 1.2 Flash increases generated video length to 15 seconds from 10 and cuts the developer price for 720p video by 30%, to $0.07 per second.

headline: OpenAI Hires Former Claude Code Product Lead Cat Wu
summary: OpenAI hired Cat Wu, who ran product for Claude Code until October 30. The hire adds a former leader of a key Anthropic product to OpenAI’s team.

headline: Uber Says AI Agents Booked Just Four Rides During Halloween Week
summary: Uber’s CFO said AI agents placed about 500 food orders during Halloween week, but only four rides. The company fulfilled about 320 million rides and Uber Eats orders during the week.

headline: Voters Reject Data Center Projects in 40 of 41 Local Ballot Measures
summary: Voters opposed data centers in 40 of 41 local ballot measures across 10 US states on November 3. In Piqua, Ohio, and Yukon, Oklahoma, voters also recalled mayors who had backed data center projects.

headline: OpenAI Publishes Community Compact for Data Center Host Towns
summary: OpenAI published a set of commitments for communities hosting its data centers, including paying the full cost of the power its sites use and publicly reporting each site’s water and energy use.

headline: UK Ministers Override Local Objections to Data Center Projects
summary: UK ministers have overridden a council’s refusal of a data center in Abbots Langley, Hertfordshire, and previously took a 300MW site in Buckinghamshire out of the council’s hands.

headline: Claude Helps Create a Parody of “Hurt”
summary: An X user used Claude to build a synthetic vocal-tube emulator, producing a parody of the song “Hurt.”

headline: OpenAI Closes $11 Billion First Tranche at $1.25 Trillion Valuation
summary: OpenAI closed an $11 billion first tranche of its funding round at a $1.25 trillion valuation, below its original target of around $30 billion or more at $1.4 trillion. The round may reach $20 billion in the coming weeks.

headline: Anthropic Takes Over $3.4 Billion Order for Gas Generators
summary: Anthropic signed a $3.4 billion deal for 1.7 gigawatts of gas-fired generators, taking over equipment orders and installation work previously arranged by power supplier OnePWR. The move gives Anthropic generation equipment rather than a power contract.

headline: Trump Says He Does Not “Mind Guardrails” on AI
summary: Donald Trump said he does not “mind guardrails” on AI, provided the US is not left in a “deep second position.”

headline: DeepSeek Says Harness Agent Reached 1.54 Million Daily Users
summary: DeepSeek said its Harness agent reached 1.54 million daily users and processed 92 trillion tokens a day.

headline: OpenAI Partners With Hacktron to Find Vulnerabilities
summary: OpenAI brought in security firm Hacktron to hunt for vulnerabilities in its own systems and integrations.

headline: Nvidia, SK Telecom and Rebellions Sign AI Computing MoU
summary: Nvidia, SK Telecom and Rebellions signed an MoU to connect Korean NPUs to Nvidia racks through NVLink Fusion.

headline: Two Chinese Firms Approved for Nvidia H200s Reportedly Have Empty Offices
summary: Two Chinese firms cleared to buy restricted Nvidia H200 chips appear to operate out of empty offices, raising questions about the approvals.

headline: US Computer and Chip Imports Reach $86.9 Billion in September
summary: US computer and chip imports hit $86.9 billion in September, equivalent to a $1.04 trillion annualized pace.

headline: AI Companies Price More Than $300 Billion in Stock and Convertibles
summary: AI companies priced more than $300 billion of stock and convertible securities in 2026, with another $100 billion queued.

headline: Accel Reportedly Leads $5 Billion Thinking Machines Lab Round
summary: Accel is reportedly leading a $5 billion funding round for Thinking Machines Lab at a $40 billion valuation.

headline: Agility Robotics Goes Public on Nasdaq
summary: Agility Robotics went public on Nasdaq, bringing renewed attention to the economics of humanoid robots.

headline: A 1,023-Parameter Edit Boosts Qwen3.5 by 29.45 Points on MATH-500
summary: Researchers reported that a direct weight edit using 1,023 parameters improved Qwen3.5’s MATH-500 score by 29.45 points.

headline: METR Reviews Anthropic Risk Report’s Automated R&D Section
summary: METR published a review of the automated R&D section of Anthropic’s August risk report.

headline: Ai2’s StateBench Finds Frontier Models Struggle to Track State Changes
summary: Ai2 introduced StateBench, a test of whether models can track state changes across long documents, and reported that frontier models struggle with the task.

headline: Ai2 Releases ToyBlocks Simulation Environment for Robot Learning
summary: Ai2 released ToyBlocks, an open simulation environment for robot learning and evaluation.

headline: Google Releases Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash
summary: Google’s Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash extends generated clips to 15 seconds, lowers 720p pricing by 30% to $0.07 per second, and adds conversational editing. It is generally available in the Gemini API and Google Cloud.

headline: Perplexity Launches Persistent Teammates Agents
summary: Perplexity launched Teammates, persistent agents that continue working between sessions, exclusive to its $200-a-month Max plan. Mobile access is promised later.

headline: Google ADK 2.14.0 Graduates Modules From Experimental
summary: Google’s Agent Development Kit reached version 2.14.0, moving a large batch of authentication, environment and toolset modules out of experimental status.

headline: Thinking Machines Announces Inkling 2 Small, With Weights Pending
summary: Thinking Machines announced Inkling 2 Small, a 594B-parameter model with 17B active parameters, claiming improvements in agentic coding and vision. The model launched with closed weights, which are promised in the coming weeks pending additional safety testing.

headline: Mistral Launches Studio
summary: Mistral launched Studio alongside its Le Chonk release.

headline: Hugging Face Releases Phonon TTS for On-Device Speech
summary: Hugging Face released Phonon TTS, a text-to-speech tool designed for on-device use.

headline: Clive Lets AIs Set iPhone Alarms
summary: Clive lets Claude and other AI assistants set alarms on an iPhone.

headline: Obsiva Turns Site Photos and Voice Notes Into Inspection Reports
summary: Obsiva turns site photos and voice notes into a PDF inspection report.

headline: MuJoCo 4 Adds a Studio to Its Robotics Physics Engine
summary: MuJoCo 4 is a robotics physics engine with its own studio.

headline: Inspo by Context.dev Brings Website Inspiration to Coding Agents
summary: Inspo by Context.dev provides real website inspiration for coding agents.

headline: Daytwo Lets Teams Edit Custom Sites Without Code
summary: Daytwo lets a team change a custom website without touching code.

headline: Seldon Launches Behavioral QA Agents
summary: Seldon offers QA agents that use products like customers do.

headline: AppuBot Offers a Free Grok Bot Alternative
summary: AppuBot is a free Grok Bot alternative that runs on your AI.

headline: ZUS Launches an AI-Native IDE
summary: ZUS is an AI-native IDE where agents code with human review.

headline: Openring Offers Open-Source Voice AI Agents
summary: Openring offers open-source voice AI agents with no platform fee.

headline: Willder Syncs Apps, Agents, and Teams
summary: Willder provides a context layer that syncs apps, agents, and teams.

headline: Learning Heterogeneous Tactile Representation for General Dexterous Manipulation
summary: Robbyant researchers introduce LingBot-Touch, a tactile foundation model that learns a unified representation across different sensor types. Its plug-and-play tactile tokens improve manipulation policies, including diffusion policies and vision-language-action models.

headline: WorldFoundry: Towards Unified Infrastructure for World Intelligence
summary: OpenEnvision presents WorldFoundry, open-source infrastructure for reproducible inference and evaluation of generative world models across video, 3D/4D, embodied action, and interactive systems. Its catalog includes 270 model entries, 74 benchmarks, and 62 registered metric entries, with evidence recorded separately from evaluation claims.

headline: Sage-Taiyi: A Metacognitive Architecture for Scientific Discovery
summary: Shanghai AI Laboratory introduces Sage-Taiyi, a metacognition-inspired system that uses accumulated scientific understanding to guide research questions and methods. It ranked first on all eight Taiyi-Bench metrics and reported experimental results including raising the yield of cobalt-catalyzed carbonylation from trace amounts to 84%.

headline: Reframe: Observation-Aligned Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation for Agentic Visual Reasoning
summary: Researchers at Nanjing University introduce Reframe, a two-stage post-training framework that aligns visual agents’ observation states using evidence-aware reinforcement learning and observation-gated distillation. Across 14 image and video benchmarks, it outperformed Mix-RL and vanilla MOPD.

headline: Flide: Accelerating Decision Inference with Exact State Forking
summary: Researchers at the National University of Singapore present Flide, an inference engine for decision-model LLM agents that uses exact state forking to reduce computation overhead. Evaluations found it answered queries up to 9.5 times faster than vLLM and SGLang while staying closest to a float32 reference in total variation distance.

headline: Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2
summary: Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 with improvements in coding, reasoning, and vision. The models generate output up to 30% faster and cost less.

headline: Meta Introduces Muse Ember
summary: Meta introduced Muse Ember, a small reasoning model optimized for agent tasks such as tool calling, coding, and document parsing. Meta claims it matches Claude Haiku 5.5's highest reasoning score at roughly one-third the cost and outperforms GPT-6 Luna across reasoning settings.

headline: Google Introduces TPU 8i Max and TPU 8tx
summary: Google introduced TPU 8i Max for massive context windows and higher compute density, alongside TPU 8tx for secure and confidential inference.

headline: Anthropic Plans to Proceed With IPO Despite Market Jitters
summary: Anthropic is preparing to proceed with its IPO despite current fears in the AI sector, according to a report. Shares could begin trading as soon as Thursday next week.

headline: Adobe and Disney Sign Multi-Year AI Deal
summary: Adobe signed a multi-year deal with Disney to build custom AI models trained on Disney characters and visual styles. The companies are working on uses spanning theme parks, film, and ESPN.

headline: Instagram Launches Effect Builder for AI Stories Effects
summary: Instagram launched Effect Builder, a free web tool that lets U.S. users create AI Stories effects from text prompts. Effects can be used by others after passing a safety review.

headline: Fireworks Confirms Cyberattack Exposing Customer Data and Models
summary: Open-source AI hosting startup Fireworks confirmed a cyberattack that exposed billing details and parts of some customers’ models and datasets. The incident came days before the company planned to begin raising funds at a valuation of more than $30 billion.

headline: Nvidia Lawyer Reportedly Emailed Agents in Chip-Smuggling Investigation
summary: Nvidia’s top lawyer reportedly emailed agents investigating whether Singapore’s Megaspeed smuggled Nvidia chips to China. The Commerce Department halted the case and handed it to the Justice Department.

headline: OpenAI's Coding Agent Can Run Tasks Across Multiple Machines
summary: OpenAI added support for connecting multiple computers to one coding agent and assigning tasks to specific machines. This lets the agent handle work such as testing on a second Mac while the user continues coding on their own computer.

headline: OpenAI's Control Room Can Halt Research Model Output
summary: OpenAI's Control Room centrally authorizes research inference requests and can stop a workload's model output within 35 seconds of intervention.

headline: MoneyPrinterTurbo Automates Short-Form Video Creation From a Keyword
summary: The open-source MoneyPrinterTurbo tool generates short-form videos from a single keyword.

headline: Suno Open-Sources Bark Text-to-Audio Model
summary: Suno open-sourced Bark, a text-to-audio model that generates speech, music, and sound effects.

headline: Self-Improving 27B Model Triples Terminal Task Success Rate
summary: A paper reports that recursive rewriting helped a 27B model triple its success rate on terminal tasks.

headline: Tencent's 27B Model Reaches 125 Tokens per Second on an RTX 3090
summary: A Tencent 27B model configuration using speculative decoding reportedly reaches 125 tokens per second on an RTX 3090.

headline: Open-Source Tool Plants Fake Code to Trap AI Reverse-Engineering Attacks
summary: An open-source tool plants fake code intended to trap AI reverse-engineering attacks.

headline: OpenAI Reportedly Raises $11 Billion At $1.25 Trillion Valuation
summary: OpenAI reportedly secured $11 billion in a new funding round at a $1.25 trillion valuation, with the round potentially reaching $20 billion before closing. The amount fell short of its previously reported $30 billion fundraising target amid growing investor uncertainty around AI valuations.

headline: A Year as a Research Engineer Working on RSI at Meta
summary: A Meta research engineer describes working on recursive self-improvement (RSI), teaching agents to solve difficult problems and train future models. The post also discusses entering AI research and the skills required for research engineering.

headline: OpenAI's Internal AI R&D Time Horizons
summary: OpenAI's report on research automation finds that models still struggle to do its R&D work, despite agents increasingly solving more complex tasks for researchers. Reliability remains low, and the post considers possible explanations.

headline: Ace Is a Tool for Building Software Together, Locally
summary: Ace lets developers collaborate with agents and teammates from their own machines, without exposing work to the public internet. Agents run with the host user's privileges and can execute shell commands and modify files beyond the project.

headline: Introducing the New Auto and Auto Code Routers
summary: OpenRouter launched a next-generation Auto Router and Auto Code, a router specialized for coding work. The new Auto Router reportedly outperforms the previous version by up to 4x and chooses models using request factors alongside live pricing, provider health, and cache status.

headline: Microsoft Research's AI Frontiers Reorganized Into Microsoft AI
summary: AI Frontiers, a sub-organization within Microsoft Research that organized research efforts and pioneered work on agents, was reorganized into Microsoft AI in early September.

headline: What Does a Positive AI Future Look Like?
summary: Patrick Collison questions how work, resource allocation, and human control would function in a positive AI future. He also raises questions about how assigning moral worth to vast numbers of AIs could affect human interests under utilitarianism.

headline: Meta Introduces Custom Spaces in Muse
summary: Meta introduced Spaces in its Muse app, where users can create personalized interactive experiences by describing what they want, such as gift trackers, games, or project planners.

headline: Warp Sciences Raises $215M for AI-Powered Labs
summary: Warp Sciences raised a $215 million Series A led by Lightspeed to accelerate drug discovery using AI and robotics.

headline: Project Eve: Claude Plays MMORPGs
summary: Anthropic explored AI participation in MMORPGs, using Claude to test complex decision-making in EVE Online and EVE Frontier.

headline: Symbiotic Firms Built Around Humans and AI
summary: The article argues that firms should build their operations around human experts and AI agents from the start.

headline: Can LLMs Redesign Themselves as They Train?
summary: The article discusses how coding agents could be integrated into the training loop to redesign LLM architectures and address limitations such as compositionality and generalization.

headline: AI R&D Is Accelerating Toward Potential RSI in 2027
summary: The analysis estimates that AI is accelerating AI R&D at Anthropic, putting the company several months ahead of the AI 2027 timeline. It argues that full recursive self-improvement may be less than a year away and urges preparation for critical events in 2027 or 2028.

headline: When Will the US Become a Net Importer of Tokens?
summary: The US could become a net importer of AI tokens between 2028 and 2030, according to an analysis of domestic capacity and demand growth. Faster demand growth or canceled data center projects could push computation overseas.

headline: Will Anthropic Grow Into Its Compute Bill?
summary: Anthropic would need an estimated $200 billion in annual revenue to support its average compute commitments through 2030 at current spending ratios. Its $895 billion in total commitments exposes it to demand shortfalls, margin compression, delivery delays, and costly short-term capacity.

headline: Two Kinds of Test-Time Scaling
summary: The essay distinguishes test-time scaling limited by the per-task compute seen during training from approaches that extend beyond training-time compute and performance. It argues that the latter could have a larger impact.

headline: What Objective Is Reasoning Solving?
summary: The analysis describes reasoning as pathfinding through possible token sequences, with success emerging from the distribution of paths. It argues that reinforcement learning raises success probability and that gains attributed to longer thinking may come from search paid for during training.

headline: NVIDIA Introduces Hardware-Aware LLM Compression
summary: NVIDIA's AutoCompress framework optimizes LLM pruning for hardware-specific latency, throughput, and memory constraints rather than parameter counts alone. It compressed Nemotron 3.5 Super from 120B to 74B parameters while retaining performance.

headline: Anthropic Secures $3.4 Billion in Gas Generators
summary: Anthropic reportedly secured 1.7 gigawatts of Caterpillar gas generators for $3.4 billion, taking over equipment orders from supplier OnePWR. The purchase expands the AI lab's investment in physical infrastructure amid power constraints and long grid-connection queues.

headline: Apple Introduces $50 AI Usage Packs in Logic Pro
summary: Apple now sells $49.99 Intelligence Usage Packs in Logic Pro to extend access to cloud-based AI features after users reach their limits. Unused capacity rolls over monthly but expires after 12 months, and packs cannot be shared through Family Sharing.

headline: Fireworks Traces October Security Incident to Cybercriminal Group
summary: Fireworks traced the October 6 unauthorized use of internal credentials to a financially motivated cybercriminal group that sells unauthorized access to large language models through illicit routing gateways.

headline: NVIDIA Presents GR00T 2 World-Action Models
summary: GR00T 2 is a new generation of foundation world-action models that can predict future video and robot actions together.

headline: ChatGPT Enterprise Comes to AWS Marketplace
summary: OpenAI made ChatGPT Enterprise available through AWS Marketplace, letting organizations purchase and manage subscriptions through existing AWS billing relationships and apply eligible spending toward AWS commitments.
